sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and file location
sections.what: Loads the build tools and creates a require function for this module. Also works out the folder this file lives in, so paths resolve correctly no matter where the command runs from.
sections.why: Likely reason: the pino plugin needs require to find its dependencies, as the comment states.

sections.name: buildAll (part 1)
sections.title: Clearing output and bundling the server
sections.what: Removes the old dist folder, then starts the bundling of src/index.ts into ES module output. Lists the heavy, native and cloud packages that stay outside the bundle so Node.js loads them at runtime.
sections.why: The comments say these packages use native code or load files by path, so bundling them breaks them.
sections.watch_out: Every package on the external list must be installed in production, or the built server will fail to start.

sections.name: buildAll (part 2)
sections.title: Logging plugin, compatibility header and error exit
sections.what: Adds the pino logging plugin with pretty output and a header that restores require, __filename and __dirname for older packages. If anything fails, prints the error and exits with a failure code.
sections.why: The comments say pino uses worker threads, so the plugin handles it instead of leaving it external. The header is there for CommonJS packages such as express.
sections.watch_out: The pdf-parse entry must stay external because it loads a worker file by path; bundling it breaks PDF reading.

summary: Build script that packs the API server's TypeScript source into one runnable JavaScript file for Node.js.
purpose: Turns the server's entry source file into dist/index.mjs, the file the server starts from, after clearing out the previous build.
why: Bundling everything into one file lets the server start from a single output file. Likely reason: the comments explain that some packages cannot be bundled, so they are left outside the output and loaded at runtime.
how: Deletes the old dist folder. Runs esbuild on src/index.ts, targeting Node.js with ES module output and bundling on. Leaves a long list of native, database, cloud and heavy packages outside the bundle. Adds the pino logging plugin. Adds a header so CommonJS-style packages still find require, __filename and __dirname. If the build throws, prints the error and exits with a failure code.
inputs: The TypeScript entry file src/index.ts, the installed npm packages, and the esbuild and pino plugin settings in this file.
outputs: dist/index.mjs with a linked source map, plus any other files esbuild writes into dist.
risks: Adding a package to the external list without it being installed at runtime makes the server fail to start. Removing a package from the list can bundle code that loads files by path, which breaks it (the pdf-parse comment describes this). The header must stay or CommonJS packages break.
debug: Run the build script and read the console output from esbuild. If start fails with a missing module, check whether that package is on the external list and installed in node_modules. If a bundled package fails at runtime, check the comments near the external list for known path problems.
